overview.headline: How the Electoral College elects the president

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the Electoral College is a process for choosing the president, not a place.
keyPoints.quote: The Electoral College is a process, not a place.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the Electoral College consists of 538 electors who choose the president.
keyPoints.quote: The Electoral College consists of 538 electors.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a majority of 270 electoral votes is required to elect the President.
keyPoints.quote: A majority of 270 electoral votes is required to elect the President.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that each state has the same number of electors as members in its congressional delegation.
keyPoints.quote: Your State has the same number of electors as it does Members in its Congressional delegation

keyPoints.point: Students learn that most states have a system that awards all electors to the candidate winning the popular vote.
keyPoints.quote: Most States have a “winner-take-all” system that awards all electors to the Presidential candidate who wins the State's popular vote.

keyTerms.gloss: Process used to elect the President and Vice President
keyTerms.quote: The Electoral College is a process, not a place.

keyTerms.gloss: Individuals chosen to cast electoral votes for president
keyTerms.quote: The Electoral College consists of 538 electors.

keyTerms.gloss: House members plus senators determining state electors
keyTerms.quote: Your State has the same number of electors as it does Members in its Congressional delegation

keyTerms.gloss: Document listing the names of appointed electors in a state
keyTerms.quote: your State's Executive prepares a Certificate of Ascertainment listing the names

keyTerms.gloss: System that awards all electors to the candidate winning the popular vote
keyTerms.quote: Most States have a “winner-take-all” system that awards all electors to the Presidential candidate who wins the State's popular vote.
